recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit. No FHIR core follow-up is needed for FHIR-13222 unless Pharmacy separately wants new R6-era dosage examples as an editorial improvement.
issue_request: FHIR-13222 asked when complex administration, timing, tapering, and relationship instructions should be represented in Dosage.text versus Dosage.additionalInstruction, and whether additionalInstruction should also appear in the free-text dosage instruction. Pharmacy resolved that all submitted examples except the prescribed drug name belong in dosage.text, while Dosage.additionalInstruction is intended to be coded and may include text when no code exists.
initial_application: Commit 36e1ed2f5f126b7641b3e1961589013cff52ea12 applied TR#13222 to the Dosage spreadsheet source by expanding Dosage.additionalInstruction examples and requirements, adding the coded-with-text-fallback guidance, and adding a comment that administration/preparation details should be populated in dosage.text.
additional_context: Dosage remains an active normative datatype in source/fhir.ini. The later combined-branch FHIR-39319 reconciliation clarified Dosage.text as a complete free-text dosage/SIG representation while preserving FHIR-13222's additionalInstruction guidance. A Zulip thread from the original reporter confirms Pharmacy's resolution, and no conflicting Confluence, Zulip, Jira, or git evidence was found.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/datatypes/dosage.xml already states that Dosage.text is the complete free-text/SIG representation and that administration/preparation details belong in dosage.text, while Dosage.additionalInstruction is a coded supplemental patient instruction or warning with text fallback when no code exists.
